## Jazz time {#drums-auto}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Jazz time**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Follows the Feel menu. Swing: the ride pattern, hi-hat foot on 2 and 4, a feathered kick and a little snare. Straight eighths: eighths on the cymbal, kick on 1 and 3, cross-stick on 2 and 4.

It belongs in *Swing*, *Jazz ballad*, *Boogaloo* and *Stride piano*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Jazz time","opts":{"groove":"auto"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Quarter notes (learning swing, 1)

Start with something simpler. Only the beat: the cymbal on 1, 2, 3 and 4 and the hi-hat foot on 2 and 4. No kick, no snare, no fills. The first thing to play on a blues.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter notes (learning swing, 1)","opts":{"groove":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Ride pattern (learning swing, 2)

The swing ride pattern and nothing else: the cymbal on every beat with a skip note before 3 and before 1 (ding, ding-a, ding, ding-a), and the hi-hat foot on 2 and 4.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-ridetime) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Ride pattern (learning swing, 2)","opts":{"groove":"ridetime"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Jazz time, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The ride pattern with a feathered kick on every beat (felt more than heard) and a few snare comments. Add one limb at a time to the ride pattern.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Jazz time","opts":{"groove":"auto"}},{"label":"Ride pattern (learning swing, 2) (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"ridetime"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums bass" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Jazz time","opts":{"groove":"auto"}}]'></div>

It is one of the first patterns to learn, so this page starts from it and takes it into the band. ### The pattern

Only the beat: the cymbal on 1, 2, 3 and 4 and the hi-hat foot on 2 and 4. No kick, no snare, no fills. The first thing to play on a blues.

It belongs in *Swing*, *Jazz ballad*, *Stride piano* and *Boogie-woogie*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

## Blues shuffle {#drums-shuffle}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Blues shuffle**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Swung eighths all the way through on the cymbal, kick on 1 and 3 and a full snare on 2 and 4. The Chicago blues beat.

It belongs in *Swing*, *12/8 doo-wop*, *Boogie-woogie* and *Jump blues*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Blues shuffle","opts":{"groove":"shuffle"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Ride pattern (learning swing, 2)

Start with something simpler. The swing ride pattern and nothing else: the cymbal on every beat with a skip note before 3 and before 1 (ding, ding-a, ding, ding-a), and the hi-hat foot on 2 and 4.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-ridetime) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="68" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Ride pattern (learning swing, 2)","opts":{"groove":"ridetime"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Hi-hat: quarter notes

Closed hi-hat on every beat, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The first rock beat. In 3/4: hi-hat on every beat, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-hhquarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="68" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: quarter notes","opts":{"groove":"hhquarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Blues shuffle, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Swung eighths on the cymbal all the way through, kick on 1 and 3, a full snare on 2 and 4. The Chicago blues beat: heavier than jazz time.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="68" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Blues shuffle","opts":{"groove":"shuffle"}},{"label":"Hi-hat: quarter notes (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"hhquarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 96 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums bass" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Blues shuffle","opts":{"groove":"shuffle"}}]'></div>

## Jump blues {#drums-jump}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Jump blues**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The blues shuffle pushed harder: swung eighths on the cymbal, the kick feathered on all four beats, and a loud backbeat on the snare on 2 and 4. In 3/4 the snare on 2 and 3.

It belongs in *Jump blues* and *Boogie-woogie*. Here it is in the jump blues style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="jump" data-chart="C7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="160" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Jump blues","opts":{"groove":"jump"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Blues shuffle

Start with something simpler. Swung eighths all the way through on the cymbal, kick on 1 and 3 and a full snare on 2 and 4. The Chicago blues beat.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-shuffle) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="jump" data-chart="C7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="112" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Blues shuffle","opts":{"groove":"shuffle"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Jump blues, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The blues shuffle, harder: swung eighths on the cymbal, the snare hit hard on 2 and 4, and the kick played softly on all four beats (feathered: felt more than heard). Get the shuffle steady, then add the kick on 2 and 4 under the snare, quietly.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="jump" data-chart="C7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="112" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Jump blues","opts":{"groove":"jump"}},{"label":"Blues shuffle (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"shuffle"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 160 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="jump" data-chart="C7|F7|C7|G7" data-tempo="160" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums bass" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Jump blues","opts":{"groove":"jump"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

## Funk {#drums-funk}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Funk**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Snare on 2 and 4 with a syncopated kick: beat 1, the and of 2 and the and of 3. Eighths on the cymbal.

It belongs in *Boogaloo* and *Straight-eighth rock*. Here it is in the boogaloo style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Funk","opts":{"groove":"funk"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Hi-hat: eighth notes

Start with something simpler. Closed hi-hat on every eighth note, all of one weight, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The basic rock beat. In 3/4: six eighths, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-hheighths) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="78" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: eighth notes","opts":{"groove":"hheighths"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Rock backbeat

Eighths on the cymbal and a full snare on 2 and 4. The kick changes over four bars: 1, 3 and the and of 3; then 1, the and of 2 and 3; the last bar adds a pickup on the and of 4. Sixteenth-note fills.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-rock) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="78" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Rock backbeat","opts":{"groove":"rock"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Funk, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Snare on 2 and 4, eighths on the cymbal, and a syncopated kick: 1, the and of 2, the and of 3. Practise the kick against the hat alone first.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="78" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Funk","opts":{"groove":"funk"}},{"label":"Rock backbeat (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"rock"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="boogaloo" data-chart="F7|F7|Bb7|F7" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums bass" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Funk","opts":{"groove":"funk"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same drum groove in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Straight-eighth rock**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Funk","opts":{"groove":"funk"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Hi-hat: eighth notes](drums.qmd#drums-hheighths), [Rock backbeat](drums.qmd#drums-rock).
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Boogaloo riff](bass.qmd#bass-riff) (bass line), [Boogaloo riff, walking at times](bass.qmd#bass-riffwalk) (bass line), [Boogaloo stabs](chords.qmd#chords-stabs) (comping rhythm).
- **Plays with, in boogaloo:** [Boogaloo riff](bass.qmd#bass-riff) (bass line), [Boogaloo stabs](chords.qmd#chords-stabs) (comping rhythm), [Tumbao](congas.qmd#congas-tumbao) (conga part).
- **Other drum grooves in the Jazz group:** [Jazz time](drums.qmd#drums-auto), [Quarter notes (learning swing, 1)](drums.qmd#drums-quarters), [Ride pattern (learning swing, 2)](drums.qmd#drums-ridetime), [Blues shuffle](drums.qmd#drums-shuffle), [Jump blues](drums.qmd#drums-jump), [Hi-hat: swing time](drums.qmd#drums-hhswing).

## Hi-hat: swing time {#drums-hhswing}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Hi-hat: swing time**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The ride pattern played on the hi-hat itself: open on 1 and 3, closed on 2 and 4 with the skip note after them, the foot closing the cymbals on 2 and 4. Swung. Nothing else.

It belongs in *Swing*, *Stride piano* and *Boogie-woogie*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: swing time","opts":{"groove":"hhswing"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Quarter notes (learning swing, 1)

Start with something simpler. Only the beat: the cymbal on 1, 2, 3 and 4 and the hi-hat foot on 2 and 4. No kick, no snare, no fills. The first thing to play on a blues.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter notes (learning swing, 1)","opts":{"groove":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Ride pattern (learning swing, 2)

The swing ride pattern and nothing else: the cymbal on every beat with a skip note before 3 and before 1 (ding, ding-a, ding, ding-a), and the hi-hat foot on 2 and 4.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-ridetime) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Ride pattern (learning swing, 2)","opts":{"groove":"ridetime"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Hi-hat: swing time, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The ride pattern played on the hi-hat: open on 1 and 3, closed on 2 and 4 with the skip note. The foot closes the cymbals on 2 and 4.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: swing time","opts":{"groove":"hhswing"}},{"label":"Ride pattern (learning swing, 2) (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"ridetime"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums bass" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: swing time","opts":{"groove":"hhswing"}}]'></div>

The same drum groove in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Stride piano**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="stride" data-chart="C|A7|D7|G7" data-tempo="132" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: swing time","opts":{"groove":"hhswing"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Plays with, in swing:** [Walking](bass.qmd#bass-walk) (bass line), [Varied](chords.qmd#chords-auto) (comping rhythm).
- **Other drum grooves in the Jazz group:** [Jazz time](drums.qmd#drums-auto), [Quarter notes (learning swing, 1)](drums.qmd#drums-quarters), [Ride pattern (learning swing, 2)](drums.qmd#drums-ridetime), [Blues shuffle](drums.qmd#drums-shuffle), [Jump blues](drums.qmd#drums-jump), [Funk](drums.qmd#drums-funk).

## Son clave (2-3) {#drums-clave}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Son clave (2-3)**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The 2-3 son clave on the cross-stick over two bars, a bell pattern on the cymbal and a light kick with the tumbao bass. A drum-kit part for the clave and timbales of a real section; the congas are a player of their own.

It belongs in *Son montuno*. Here it is in the son montuno style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="montuno" data-chart="C|F|G7|C" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Son clave (2-3)","opts":{"groove":"clave"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Hi-hat: quarter notes

Start with something simpler. Closed hi-hat on every beat, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The first rock beat. In 3/4: hi-hat on every beat, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-hhquarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

**How to play it.** The 2-3 son clave on the cross-stick over two bars (2 and 3, then 1, the and of 2, 4), a bell pattern on the cymbal, a light kick. Clap the clave first.

## Bo Diddley beat {#drums-bodiddley}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Bo Diddley beat**. ### The pattern

The 3-2 clave played on the toms over a steady kick: 1, the and of 2, 4, then 2 and 3. Faith, Desire, I Want Candy.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

## Waltz in one {#drums-waltz}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Waltz in one**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

For a quick 3/4: kick on 1, a brushed snare on 2 and 3. Four bars make one phrase: the kick leans on the first and third, the snare answers in the second and fourth, and the fourth leads back in. In 4/4 it is the two-beat.

It belongs in *Waltz (in one)*, *Boom-chick* and *Folk carol*. Here it is in the waltz (in one) style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="150" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-meter="3/4" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Waltz in one","opts":{"groove":"waltz"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Two-beat

Start with something simpler. Kick with the bass on 1 and 3, a soft snare with the chords on 2 and 4. In 3/4: kick on 1, snare on 2 and 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-boomchick) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

**How to play it.** Kick on 1, brushed snare on 2 and 3, felt in one. Lean on the first and third bars of each four-bar phrase.

## Rock backbeat {#drums-rock}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Rock backbeat**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Eighths on the cymbal and a full snare on 2 and 4. The kick changes over four bars: 1, 3 and the and of 3; then 1, the and of 2 and 3; the last bar adds a pickup on the and of 4. Sixteenth-note fills.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock* and *Emo / pop-punk*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Rock backbeat","opts":{"groove":"rock"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Hi-hat: quarter notes

Start with something simpler. Closed hi-hat on every beat, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The first rock beat. In 3/4: hi-hat on every beat, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-hhquarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: quarter notes","opts":{"groove":"hhquarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Hi-hat: eighth notes

Closed hi-hat on every eighth note, all of one weight, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The basic rock beat. In 3/4: six eighths, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-hheighths) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: eighth notes","opts":{"groove":"hheighths"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Rock backbeat, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Eighths on the hat, full snare on 2 and 4, and a kick that changes over four bars: 1, 3 and the and of 3; then 1, the and of 2 and 3; the last bar adds a pickup on the and of 4.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Rock backbeat","opts":{"groove":"rock"}},{"label":"Hi-hat: eighth notes (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"hheighths"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums bass" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Rock backbeat","opts":{"groove":"rock"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same drum groove in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Emo / pop-punk**

## Pop backbeat {#drums-strum}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Pop backbeat**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A lighter backbeat for a strummed song: kick on 1, the and of 2 and 3, with the Dotted bass line. Fills are a snare note or two.

It belongs in *Acoustic strum*, *Straight-eighth rock* and *Piano ballad*. Here it is in the acoustic strum style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Pop backbeat","opts":{"groove":"strum"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Hi-hat: eighth notes

Start with something simpler. Closed hi-hat on every eighth note, all of one weight, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The basic rock beat. In 3/4: six eighths, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-hheighths) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

### Step 2: Pop backbeat, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** A lighter backbeat: kick on 1, the and of 2 and 3 (with the dotted bass line), snare on 2 and 4. Fills are a snare note or two.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Pop backbeat","opts":{"groove":"strum"}},{"label":"Hi-hat: eighth notes (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"hheighths"}}]'></div>

The whole band, at 96 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

## Ballad {#drums-ballad}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Ballad**. Quiet eighths on the cymbal, a cross-stick on 2 and 4 and a soft kick on 1, the and of 2 and 3. In a chorus bar the cross-stick becomes the snare.

It belongs in *Piano ballad* and *Acoustic strum*. Here it is in the piano ballad style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

Start with something simpler. Closed hi-hat on every eighth note, all of one weight, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The basic rock beat. In 3/4: six eighths, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-hheighths) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

**How to play it.** Quiet eighths on the cymbal, cross-stick on 2 and 4 (the stick laid across the snare, tapping the rim), soft kick on 1, the and of 2 and 3. Play with half the force of a rock beat.

## Four on the floor {#drums-dance}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Four on the floor**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Kick on every beat, snare and clap on 2 and 4, and the open hi-hat on every off-beat.

It belongs in *Dance pop*. Here it is in the dance pop style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Four on the floor","opts":{"groove":"dance"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Hi-hat: quarter notes

Start with something simpler. Closed hi-hat on every beat, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The first rock beat. In 3/4: hi-hat on every beat, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-hhquarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: quarter notes","opts":{"groove":"hhquarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Hi-hat: open off-beats

Four on the floor: kick on every beat, snare on 2 and 4, a closed hi-hat on each beat and an open one on every off-beat (the stick closing it each time). The Four on the floor groove without the clap.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-hhdance) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: open off-beats","opts":{"groove":"hhdance"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Four on the floor, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Kick on every beat, snare and clap on 2 and 4, open hi-hat on every off-beat. The kick must not waver.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Four on the floor","opts":{"groove":"dance"}},{"label":"Hi-hat: open off-beats (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"hhdance"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums bass" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Four on the floor","opts":{"groove":"dance"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Hi-hat: quarter notes](drums.qmd#drums-hhquarters), [Hi-hat: open off-beats](drums.qmd#drums-hhdance).
- **Leads to:** [Reggaeton (dembow)](drums.qmd#drums-dembow): the patterns that use this one as a step.
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Octaves (disco)](bass.qmd#bass-octaves) (bass line), [Hi-hat: open off-beats](drums.qmd#drums-hhdance) (drum groove).
- **Plays with, in dance pop:** [Octaves (disco)](bass.qmd#bass-octaves) (bass line), [3+3+2 (tresillo)](chords.qmd#chords-tresillo) (comping rhythm).
- **Other drum grooves in the Folk, rock and pop group:** [Bo Diddley beat](drums.qmd#drums-bodiddley), [Waltz in one](drums.qmd#drums-waltz), [Two-beat](drums.qmd#drums-boomchick), [Rock backbeat](drums.qmd#drums-rock), [Pop backbeat](drums.qmd#drums-strum), [Ballad](drums.qmd#drums-ballad), [Motown](drums.qmd#drums-motown), [Train beat](drums.qmd#drums-train).

**How to play it.** Three eighths to every beat on the cymbal, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. Count 1-and-a 2-and-a.

## Half-time {#drums-halftime}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Half-time**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The backbeat at half speed: kick on 1 and the and of 2, one snare on beat 3.

It belongs in *Piano ballad*, *Straight-eighth rock* and *Emo / pop-punk*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Half-time","opts":{"groove":"halftime"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Hi-hat: eighth notes

Start with something simpler. Closed hi-hat on every eighth note, all of one weight, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The basic rock beat. In 3/4: six eighths, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-hheighths) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: eighth notes","opts":{"groove":"hheighths"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Rock backbeat

Eighths on the cymbal and a full snare on 2 and 4. The kick changes over four bars: 1, 3 and the and of 3; then 1, the and of 2 and 3; the last bar adds a pickup on the and of 4. Sixteenth-note fills.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-rock) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Rock backbeat","opts":{"groove":"rock"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Half-time, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The backbeat at half speed: kick on 1 and the and of 2, a single snare on beat 3. The chords go as fast, the song feels slower.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Half-time","opts":{"groove":"halftime"}},{"label":"Rock backbeat (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"rock"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums bass" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Half-time","opts":{"groove":"halftime"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same drum groove in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Half-time","opts":{"groove":"halftime"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Hi-hat: off-beats only**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

The closed hi-hat plays only the ands, 1-and 2-and 3-and 4-and. Kick on every beat, snare on 2 and 4. In 3/4: kick on 1 and 2, snare on 3.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock*, *Piano ballad*, *Acoustic strum*, *Dance pop* and *Boogaloo*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: off-beats only","opts":{"groove":"hhoffbeats"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Hi-hat: eighth notes

Start with something simpler. Closed hi-hat on every eighth note, all of one weight, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The basic rock beat. In 3/4: six eighths, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-hheighths) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

### Step 2: Hi-hat: off-beats only, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** The hi-hat only on the ands, the kick on every beat, the snare on 2 and 4. The hand fills in between the foot.

## Hi-hat: one open note {#drums-hhopen}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Hi-hat: one open note**. ### The pattern

Eighth notes on the closed hi-hat, with the and of 4 left open. The foot and the stick close it again on beat 1 of the next bar. Kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock*, *Piano ballad*, *Acoustic strum*, *Dance pop* and *Boogaloo*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

Start with something simpler. Closed hi-hat on every eighth note, all of one weight, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The basic rock beat. In 3/4: six eighths, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-hheighths) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

## Hi-hat: open off-beats {#drums-hhdance}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Hi-hat: open off-beats**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Four on the floor: kick on every beat, snare on 2 and 4, a closed hi-hat on each beat and an open one on every off-beat (the stick closing it each time). The Four on the floor groove without the clap.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock*, *Piano ballad*, *Acoustic strum*, *Dance pop* and *Boogaloo*. Here it is in the dance pop style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

### Step 1: Hi-hat: eighth notes

Start with something simpler. Closed hi-hat on every eighth note, all of one weight, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The basic rock beat. In 3/4: six eighths, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-hheighths) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: eighth notes","opts":{"groove":"hheighths"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Hi-hat: off-beats only

The closed hi-hat plays only the ands, 1-and 2-and 3-and 4-and. Kick on every beat, snare on 2 and 4. In 3/4: kick on 1 and 2, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-hhoffbeats) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="84" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: off-beats only","opts":{"groove":"hhoffbeats"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Hi-hat: open off-beats, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Four on the floor: kick every beat, snare on 2 and 4, a closed hat on each beat and an open one on every and. The foot opens and closes in eighths.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock*, *Piano ballad*, *Acoustic strum*, *Dance pop* and *Boogaloo*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

## Hi-hat: foot on every beat {#drums-hhfoot4}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Hi-hat: foot on every beat**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Eighth notes on the ride cymbal, the hi-hat closed with the foot on all four beats, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock*, *Piano ballad*, *Acoustic strum*, *Dance pop* and *Boogaloo*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: foot on every beat","opts":{"groove":"hhfoot4"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Hi-hat: eighth notes

Start with something simpler. Closed hi-hat on every eighth note, all of one weight, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The basic rock beat. In 3/4: six eighths, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-hheighths) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: eighth notes","opts":{"groove":"hheighths"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Hi-hat: foot on every beat, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Eighths on the ride, the hi-hat closed by the foot on all four beats, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. Four limbs, each with its own job.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: foot on every beat","opts":{"groove":"hhfoot4"}},{"label":"Hi-hat: eighth notes (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"hheighths"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums bass" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: foot on every beat","opts":{"groove":"hhfoot4"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same drum groove in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="pop" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: foot on every beat","opts":{"groove":"hhfoot4"}}]'></div>

**Acoustic strum**

**Dance pop**

- **Builds on:** [Hi-hat: eighth notes](drums.qmd#drums-hheighths).
- **Plays with, in straight-eighth rock:** [Root eighths](bass.qmd#bass-eighths) (bass line), [Strum: down-up eighths](chords.qmd#chords-strum-eights) (comping rhythm).
- **Other drum grooves in the Folk, rock and pop group:** [Bo Diddley beat](drums.qmd#drums-bodiddley), [Waltz in one](drums.qmd#drums-waltz), [Two-beat](drums.qmd#drums-boomchick), [Rock backbeat](drums.qmd#drums-rock), [Pop backbeat](drums.qmd#drums-strum), [Ballad](drums.qmd#drums-ballad), [Four on the floor](drums.qmd#drums-dance), [Motown](drums.qmd#drums-motown).

## Reggaeton (dembow) {#drums-dembow}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Reggaeton (dembow)**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Kick on every beat, with the snare on the sixteenth before beats 2 and 4 and on the and of 2 and 4: a 3+3+2 in sixteenths, twice a bar. Despacito, One Dance.

It belongs in *Reggaeton* and *Dance pop*. Here it is in the reggaeton style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="reggaeton" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="92" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Reggaeton (dembow)","opts":{"groove":"dembow"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Hi-hat: quarter notes

Start with something simpler. Closed hi-hat on every beat, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. The first rock beat. In 3/4: hi-hat on every beat, kick on 1, snare on 3.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-hhquarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="reggaeton" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="64" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Hi-hat: quarter notes","opts":{"groove":"hhquarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Four on the floor

Kick on every beat, snare and clap on 2 and 4, and the open hi-hat on every off-beat.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-dance) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="reggaeton" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="64" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Four on the floor","opts":{"groove":"dance"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Reggaeton (dembow), slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Kick on every beat; snare on the sixteenth before 2 and 4 and on the and of 2 and 4: 3+3+2 in sixteenths, twice a bar. Learn the snare against the kick slowly.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="reggaeton" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="64" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Reggaeton (dembow)","opts":{"groove":"dembow"}},{"label":"Four on the floor (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"dance"}}]'></div>

### Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 92 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="reggaeton" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="92" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums bass" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Reggaeton (dembow)","opts":{"groove":"dembow"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same drum groove in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Dance pop**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="dance" data-chart="Am|F|C|G" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Reggaeton (dembow)","opts":{"groove":"dembow"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Hi-hat: quarter notes](drums.qmd#drums-hhquarters), [Four on the floor](drums.qmd#drums-dance).
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [3+3+2 (tresillo)](bass.qmd#bass-tresillo) (bass line), [3+3+2 (tresillo)](chords.qmd#chords-tresillo) (comping rhythm), [Strum: 3-3-2 accents](chords.qmd#chords-strum332) (comping rhythm), [Ballad: syncopated](chords.qmd#chords-ball-sync) (comping rhythm).
- **Plays with, in reggaeton:** [3+3+2 (tresillo)](bass.qmd#bass-tresillo) (bass line), [Long notes](chords.qmd#chords-pad) (comping rhythm).
- **Other drum grooves in the Caribbean group:** [Calypso](drums.qmd#drums-calypso), [Reggae one-drop](drums.qmd#drums-onedrop).

- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Held roots (the bass voice)](bass.qmd#bass-held) (bass line), [Roots on 1 and 3](bass.qmd#bass-halves) (bass line), [Long notes](chords.qmd#chords-pad) (comping rhythm), [Hymn: four parts](chords.qmd#chords-hymn) (comping rhythm).
- **Plays with, in folk carol:** [Roots on 1 and 3](bass.qmd#bass-halves) (bass line), [Strum: D, D-U, D, D-U](chords.qmd#chords-strum-folk) (comping rhythm).
- **Other drum grooves in the Hymns and carols group:** [Brushes, swing](drums.qmd#drums-brushswing), [Brushes, ballad](drums.qmd#drums-brushballad), [Brushes, folk](drums.qmd#drums-brushfolk).

## Brushes, swing {#drums-brushswing}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Brushes, swing**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Brushes on the snare: a swish on every beat, leaning on 2 and 4, and taps on the ride pattern (1, 2, the skip after 2, 3, 4, the skip after 4). Hi-hat foot on 2 and 4, a kick you feel more than hear. No fills.

It belongs in *Swing*, *Jazz ballad*, *Folk carol* and *Boom-chick*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Brushes, swing","opts":{"groove":"brushswing"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Ride pattern (learning swing, 2)

Start with something simpler. The swing ride pattern and nothing else: the cymbal on every beat with a skip note before 3 and before 1 (ding, ding-a, ding, ding-a), and the hi-hat foot on 2 and 4.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-ridetime) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Ride pattern (learning swing, 2)","opts":{"groove":"ridetime"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Brushes, swing, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Left hand: a circle on the snare head, a swish on every beat, a little more on 2 and 4. Right hand: the ride pattern in taps. The foot closes the hat on 2 and 4. Keep the circle going even when the taps rest.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Brushes, swing","opts":{"groove":"brushswing"}},{"label":"Ride pattern (learning swing, 2) (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"ridetime"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums bass" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Brushes, swing","opts":{"groove":"brushswing"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same drum groove in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Jazz ballad**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="ballad" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="66" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Brushes, swing","opts":{"groove":"brushswing"}}]'></div>

**Folk carol**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Brushes, swing","opts":{"groove":"brushswing"}}]'></div>

**Boom-chick**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="folk" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="104" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Brushes, swing","opts":{"groove":"brushswing"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Ride pattern (learning swing, 2)](drums.qmd#drums-ridetime).
- **Plays with, in swing:** [Walking](bass.qmd#bass-walk) (bass line), [Varied](chords.qmd#chords-auto) (comping rhythm).
- **Other drum grooves in the Hymns and carols group:** [Light time](drums.qmd#drums-brushes), [Brushes, ballad](drums.qmd#drums-brushballad), [Brushes, folk](drums.qmd#drums-brushfolk).

## Brushes, ballad {#drums-brushballad}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Brushes, ballad**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

Both brushes stir the snare, circling in opposite directions: the left hand's long sweep from 1 and from 3, the right hand's sweep leaning in on 2 and 4. A soft kick on 1, the hi-hat foot on 2 and 4. In 3/4 one long sweep to the bar and the right hand on 2 and 3. No fills.

It belongs in *Jazz ballad*, *Swing*, *Piano ballad*, *Boom-chick*, *Folk carol* and *Hymn (four parts)*. Here it is in the jazz ballad style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="ballad" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="66" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Brushes, ballad","opts":{"groove":"brushballad"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Quarter notes (learning swing, 1)

Start with something simpler. Only the beat: the cymbal on 1, 2, 3 and 4 and the hi-hat foot on 2 and 4. No kick, no snare, no fills. The first thing to play on a blues.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-quarters) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="ballad" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="50" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter notes (learning swing, 1)","opts":{"groove":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Brushes, ballad, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Both hands stir, circling in opposite directions: the left hand's long sweep landing on 1 and again on 3, the right hand's sweep leaning in on 2 and 4 (no taps). Let the sound hang; do not press the wires.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="ballad" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="50" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Brushes, ballad","opts":{"groove":"brushballad"}},{"label":"Quarter notes (learning swing, 1) (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"quarters"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 66 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="ballad" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="66" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums bass" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Brushes, ballad","opts":{"groove":"brushballad"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same drum groove in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Swing**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Brushes, ballad","opts":{"groove":"brushballad"}}]'></div>

**Boom-chick**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="folk" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="104" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Brushes, ballad","opts":{"groove":"brushballad"}}]'></div>

### How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Quarter notes (learning swing, 1)](drums.qmd#drums-quarters).
- **Plays with, in jazz ballad:** [Two-feel](bass.qmd#bass-two) (bass line), [Long notes](chords.qmd#chords-pad) (comping rhythm).
- **Other drum grooves in the Hymns and carols group:** [Light time](drums.qmd#drums-brushes), [Brushes, swing](drums.qmd#drums-brushswing), [Brushes, folk](drums.qmd#drums-brushfolk).

## Brushes, folk {#drums-brushfolk}

*For drum kit, built up a step at a time.*

This is a lesson on one drum groove the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Brushes, folk**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd)

### The pattern

A swish on every beat that leans on 2 and 4, light taps on the off-beat eighths and a soft kick on 1 and 3. A quiet country backbeat. No fills.

It belongs in *Boom-chick*, *Folk carol*, *Acoustic strum*, *John Prine Fingerpicking*, *Country train beat* and *Piano ballad*. Here it is in the boom-chick style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="folk" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="104" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Brushes, folk","opts":{"groove":"brushfolk"}}]'></div>

### Step 1: Light time

Start with something simpler. Very quiet eighths on the hi-hat, a soft kick on 1 and 3 and a light cross-stick on 2 and 4. No fills. A stand-in for brushes.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](drums.qmd#drums-brushes) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums play alone first; switch the bass and chords on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="folk" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Light time","opts":{"groove":"brushes"}}]'></div>

### Step 2: Brushes, folk, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** A swish on every beat with the weight on 2 and 4, light taps between, a soft kick on 1 and 3. It stays under the singer like Light time, with a backbeat you can hear.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="folk" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="72" data-on="drums" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Brushes, folk","opts":{"groove":"brushfolk"}},{"label":"Light time (the step before)","opts":{"groove":"brushes"}}]'></div>

### Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 104 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's drum kit off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="folk" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="104" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums bass" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Brushes, folk","opts":{"groove":"brushfolk"}}]'></div>

### In other styles

The same drum groove in other styles it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.

**Folk carol**

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="carol" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Brushes, folk","opts":{"groove":"brushfolk"}}]'></div>

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="prine" data-chart="G|C|D|G" data-tempo="100" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="drums" data-choice-label="Drum groove:" data-choices='[{"label":"Brushes, folk","opts":{"groove":"brushfolk"}}]'></div>

- **Other drum grooves in the Hymns and carols group:** [Light time](drums.qmd#drums-brushes), [Brushes, swing](drums.qmd#drums-brushswing), [Brushes, ballad](drums.qmd#drums-brushballad).
